api_analysis.hypothesis: The compiled signature exposes bias as a required non-nullable torch.Tensor, but the operator_contract allows bias to be nullable (None). The binding function signature lacks an appropriate Optional[torch.Tensor] annotation and pybind11 conversion, causing the signature checker to reject it.
evidence: interface.json error: compiled signatures differ from operator_contract; signature list shows bias: torch.Tensor without Optional/None.
custom_ops_contract.json defines bias as nullable: true.
model_new.py always passes a real bias tensor, but the contract validator checks the compiled signature, which must accept None if nullable.
The binding function uses torch::Tensor bias with no default or Optional annotation; pybind11 treats it as required tensor.
changes: Modify kernels/conv_transpose1d_binding.cpp to accept c10::optional<torch::Tensor> bias (or torch::optional) and adjust TORCH_CHECK accordingly.
Use c10::optional<torch::Tensor> bias in the binding signature; if bias.has_value() use it, else pass nullptr to launcher.
Ensure pybind11 doc signature shows Optional[torch.Tensor] or similar to satisfy validator.
Keep all other code unchanged to avoid introducing new errors.
